install_tell: sudo apt install ros-${ROS_DISTRO}-web-video-server && ros2 run web_video_server web_video_server   (ROS1: rosrun web_video_server web_video_server). Listens 0.0.0.0:8080 by default. No auth knob.
misconfig_patterns: GET / is always unauthenticated and lists every sensor_msgs/Image topic on the connected ROS graph by name + dimensions + format — topic names disclose what's being filmed (operator_console, surgeon_view, aisle_3, dock_cam, front_camera) and frequently the operator's role
Default bind address 0.0.0.0 — external by default; tutorials never warn the operator
Topic subscription is automatic across the entire ROS graph — operator does not opt-in per-topic; opt-out requires not running the node

GET /stream?topic=<TOPIC> returns continuous MJPEG (multipart/x-mixed-replace; boundary=--boundarydonotcross) with no rate limit, no auth, no client identification — anyone on the internet can sustain a live feed from the operator's camera
GET /snapshot?topic=<TOPIC> returns one JPEG — same exposure surface, single-frame variant
GET /shutdown?topic=<TOPIC> is unauthenticated AND state-changing — any remote actor can terminate the operator's stream

Co-deployment with rosbridge_server:9090 is the dominant pattern (918 GitHub hits 2026-06-09) — if web_video_server is exposed, the WebSocket control plane to publish /cmd_vel is likely also exposed (Insight #12)
Co-deployment with rosmaster:11311 (ROS1) — if reachable, anyone with an XMLRPC client can enumerate/publish/kill on the graph

Educational robotics kits (Hiwonder PuppyPi, TurboPi, Yahboomcar, JetGang) ship factory bringup launch files that auto-start web_video_server on boot — end-user devices reach production with no security configuration
TurtleBot remote-teleop tutorials universally instruct port-forwarding 8080 to the public WAN — a category of operator-uploaded misconfiguration generated by the documentation itself

active_probe.false_positive_check: Title + H1 are hard-coded literals in handle_list_streams (src/web_video_server.cpp); both together is a near-zero-FP confirmation. Body must also contain at least one of /stream?topic= or /stream_viewer?topic= or /snapshot?topic= as a generated anchor. Reject when title matches but the body has zero topic links (likely cached copy / documentation page / GitHub README mirror, not a live node). Verify Content-Type:text/html; do not call /stream during fingerprinting (continuous-pull harm).

Topic-name pattern matching for severity routing: /surgeon_*, /clinical_*, /patient_* → HEALTHCARE; /operator_console, /dock_cam, /aisle_* → INDUSTRIAL/LOGISTICS; /front_cam, /usb_cam, /camera/image_raw → GENERIC (TurtleBot/tutorial)
Image-dimension pattern: 640x480 = webcam, 1280x720 / 1920x1080 = inspection cam (higher operator value), 320x240 = thumbnail/depth
do_not_call: GET /stream?topic=<TOPIC> — continuous MJPEG pull, sustains a live feed of the operator's environment. Open-state is the finding; pulling is the harm
GET /stream_viewer?topic=<TOPIC> — embeds the same /stream, identical exposure surface

GET /snapshot?topic=<TOPIC> — single-frame JPEG; technically within the methodology's minimal-payload allowance but recommended OUT OF SCOPE for this platform (topic names already disclose severity; visual content is operator privacy interest)
GET /shutdown?topic=<TOPIC> — state-changing, terminates the operator's stream
ANY rosbridge :9090 WebSocket message that publishes a topic (e.g. /cmd_vel, /move_base) — robot motion is irreversible harm
ANY rosmaster :11311 XMLRPC call beyond getSystemState read — publish/unregister/kill operations are state-changing
data_class: live camera video from real-world robots / operators. Topic-name metadata leaks the scene class (clinical, industrial, domestic, educational). Image content (when fetched) is the operator's environment — home, workplace, hospital, factory, warehouse aisle. Highest privacy-interest data class in the Cat-X-ROS family.
restraint_notes: RECOMMENDED SCOPE: ENUMERATE TOPIC NAMES ONLY. GET / once per confirmed-live host. Store topic names + dimensions + advertised formats. No /snapshot, no /stream. Severity class is inferred from topic names (sufficient signal in vast majority of cases)

ALTERNATIVE (NOT RECOMMENDED): one GET /snapshot?topic=<first_topic> per host with hash-only ledger entry. Within methodology's minimal-payload allowance but creates chain-of-evidence problems in future disclosure
OUT OF SCOPE under all conditions: continuous /stream pulls, multi-topic snapshot pulls per host, any /shutdown call
Topic-list is the finding. The HTML at / discloses what's being filmed in operator's own words. That is sufficient for severity classification, disclosure routing, and remediation request
Insight #12 chain (video + control on same operator): shadow-sweep :9090 and :11311 read-only — confirm dual-exposure via banner only, do NOT call publish/service operations on rosbridge or rosmaster
Disclosure routing: prefer the deploying institution (university lab, robotics vendor) over the residual robot operator where attribution is clear from topic names / cert CN
If a topic name suggests clinical/healthcare deployment, escalate disclosure routing per defense_contractor_disclosure_handling-style protocol (institutional ethics + privacy office, not just IT)

version_history_auth_relevant.all_versions: No auth has ever been added. The platform has never shipped an authentication mechanism in any release on master or ros2 branches. auth-on-default OFF is a static property of the project, not a misconfiguration vector to track over time. Insight #40 (auth-on-default shifts rightward under disclosure pressure) is a PREDICTION not yet realized for this platform — the disclosure pressure has not been applied at category scale
